idiom_name: explicit &Ctx parameter; task_local!/thread_local! when a value really is ambient
implementation_notes: Rust has no component tree and no implicit call-tree propagation, so the context has to be passed explicitly (a &Ctx reference, a struct field, or generics over the context type) - which keeps dependencies visible but is exactly the threading the pattern removes elsewhere. When a value genuinely is ambient, the primitives are thread_local! for per-thread state (LocalKey::with, lazily initialised, const-initialisable when the value has no destructor) and tokio::task_local! for per-task state whose LocalKey::with/scope makes the binding a real bounded scope that code below can read without parameters. Both are hand-managed: nothing resets them at a request boundary for you.
pitfalls: A thread_local read after an .await can land on a different worker thread, so thread locals must not carry request state in async code - use task_local (or an explicit parameter).
task_local values exist only inside the binding scope: anything that outlives the with/scope block, or a task spawned to outlive it, can no longer read the value.
thread_local! values are per thread with no reset point; with a work-stealing pool each worker keeps its own copy and mutated state leaks into unrelated jobs.
